label: Adreno
explanation: The graphics chip wedged on a frame and the driver reset it - the dominant GT5P stall, usually the banked-corner depth resolve a few laps in. The DRIVER-tab dial is the real lever; the TUNING knobs below only ease the load.
driver_dial: Adreno LSD dial -> sddepth   (validated GPU-hang mitigation; try syncdraw if it persists)

label: OOM
explanation: The system used up all its RAM and had to close the emulator. Lower graphical fidelity to shrink the memory footprint.

label: SPU
explanation: The emulator's fast SPU mode couldn't translate a section of game code. A safer SPU block size usually fixes it.

label: VkLost
explanation: The GPU dropped out mid-frame and the emulator couldn't continue. Usually the same root cause as an Adreno stall.
driver_dial: Adreno LSD dial -> sddepth   (same GPU-hang root cause; DRIVER tab)

label: VkSwap
explanation: The GPU lost its display surface while presenting a frame and couldn't rebuild it. Often follows heavy GPU strain.

label: PPU
explanation: A game thread spun trying to grab a lock and couldn't make progress. Often a transient timing hiccup.

label: Silent
explanation: You pressed the R3 panic button to recover from a freeze or hang. No automatic crash cause was detected for this session.

label: Thermal
explanation: No specific crash was detected, but the device hit its thermal alarm temperature during this session - heat was the probable cause. Lower resolution to cut heat output.

label: Anti-lock
summary: Anti-lock caught a hang and the race kept going
explanation: Not a crash - this is the safety net working. The GPU wedged for a moment and the kernel keepalive net absorbed it, so the emulator recovered on its own and the session finished. The rescues count is how many times it fired this run; a high count just means the track hit the danger zone often, not that anything is broken. Nothing to fix.

label: Panic
summary: The rig reset; this row was rebuilt afterward
explanation: A kernel panic reset the device, so nothing survived to log at the moment it happened. ETK rebuilt this row at the next boot from the breadcrumb it left before the race. There is no backtrace to read - the diagnosis comes from the kernel messages leading up to the reset (the panic black box), not from this row. A panic with no lead-up in those messages is the undiagnosed silent-reset class.
